rule: On a stalled Substack publish queue, redate the backlog one-per-day by default and never let more than one post ship in a single day without explicit founder request.
check: A hard daily-send-rate-limiter in the scheduler wrapper script that rejects/holds any send once one successful publish has already occurred that day, unless an explicit founder-override flag is passed
misses: Doesn't force the positive action of redating the backlog (only blocks bursts), and can't verify that an override flag was actually authorized by the founder versus set by an agent — that's a judgment call, not a detectable one

rule: Before generating art for a piece in an existing arc/series, check sibling pieces' actual rendered style and surface any conflict with the requested style before spending image budget.
When the cost of being wrong is real, query the authoritative source directly instead of inferring its capabilities/state from indirect observation (filesystem, config, env vars).

Every claim in research content needs a numbered footnote with source/author, title, URL, published date, accessed date, confidence tier 1-5, and source class; unsourced claims must be tagged UNVERIFIED, never fabricated.
check: A lint-rule/CI-job over the research file that verifies every [^n] marker has a matching '## Footnotes' entry, and that each entry matches the required field pattern (name, quoted title, URL, two dates, tier 1-5, one of the five source-class enum values)
misses: Cannot detect a substantive claim that was never given a footnote marker in the first place (requires understanding what counts as a claim), and cannot verify the cited source is real rather than fabricated

rule: A general merge-on-green or cleanup authorization does not cover git force-push/history-rewrite; that needs its own fresh, branch-named authorization before a force-push command is issued.
check: Pattern/flag detection of --force, -f, or +refspec on a git push invocation in a Bash tool call, blocking it pending explicit confirmation regardless of any prior standing authorization language

rule: Every novel failure mode observed in any session must be recorded in the canonical FAILURE-MODES.md registry the same turn it is discovered, unasked, with the tell and working countermeasure.
When multiple genuinely-needed clarifying questions arise from the same source/investigation, ask them together in one AskUserQuestion/message round instead of serially.

In evals, a surprising pass is a prompt to audit the eval's own rules for gaps, not evidence of dishonesty; verify the actual solution artifact, not just the score, even without a specific suspected exploit.
Before hand-rolling a fix for a bounded/fixable/testable task, do a cheap discovery pass (e.g. ls -t ~/projects) to check whether a purpose-built fleet tool already covers it.
Default to cli-dispatch (start/gate/land) as the delegation primitive for farming coding work to Codex/Grok, the same reflex as spawning a subagent, rather than hand-rolling git/gh mechanics.

Obsolete/outdated PRs may be closed automatically without per-PR confirmation, but only when obsolescence is confirmed with concrete evidence (artifacts, timestamps, overlapping file sets), not merely asserted by a triage agent.
Codex runs are always ChatGPT-subscription auth, never per-token metered, so a codex run must never be cost-gated on the founder or treated as requiring an API-vs-subscription check.
When a key fact changes mid-task or the agent is stuck, consult other fleet AIs (Codex, Hermes) rather than grinding solo, and use Hermes as a second implementer, not just a critic.
